packet.headline_seed: Kidnapped Nigerian retired general dies in captivity
packet.description_seed: Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar's death highlights continuing security challenges facing parts of the country.

what: Kidnapped Nigerian retired general dies in captivity

clean_source_blocks.text: A retired Nigerian army general who had been kidnapped by gunmen in the country's north-west has died while being held captive, the military has said. Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar, who had a high-profile job as military spokesman between 2015 and 2017, was abducted with his wife while travelling in Katsina state last month. No group has said it was behind the kidnappings. The abduction and death of Abubakar highlights the continuing security challenges facing parts of north-west Nigeria, where criminal gangs known locally as "bandits" frequently carry out kidnappings for ransom, as well as cattle rustling and attacks on rural communities. Some militant jihadists have also operated in the region. An alleged militant camp in Sokoto state was the target of a US airstrike on 25 December last year.
Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar's death highlights continuing security challenges facing parts of the country.

The Katsina State Government has announced the death of retired Major General Rabe Abubakar while in the custody of bandits, describing the incident as a tragic loss to his family, the state, and the nation. LEADERSHIP reports that retired General Rabe was one-time Director of Defence Information (DDI) at the Defence Headquarters (DHQ) of Nigeria. His death comes just days after he, alongside his kidnapped wife, appeared in a viral video in which he was pleading to the State government to heed to the bandits’ demands in exchange for his freedom. In a statement issued on Saturday by the Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr. Nasiru Muazu, the State government said the retired senior military officer died from complications arising from diabetes and hypertension during his captivity.

Katsina has been one of the states most affected by the violence. Local media reported that the retired officer had been going to a wedding on 30 May when armed men attacked his vehicle and seized him, his wife and their driver. Days before news of his death emerged, a video shared on social media appeared to show Abubakar in captivity. He was seen with an apparent injury to his left leg alongside his wife and other hostages. The military said it chose not to comment publicly on the abduction while efforts to free those in captivity were being made. "In deference to ongoing rescue efforts by security agencies, the Armed Forces withheld public comment while every operational resource was deployed in the hope of securing his safe return," the statement said.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
A retired Nigerian army general who had been kidnapped by gunmen in the country's north-west has died while being held captive, the military has said.

Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar, who had a high-profile job as military spokesman between 2015 and 2017, was abducted with his wife while travelling in Katsina state last month.

No group has said it was behind the kidnappings.

The abduction and death of Abubakar highlights the continuing security challenges facing parts of north-west Nigeria, where criminal gangs known locally as "bandits" frequently carry out kidnappings for ransom, as well as cattle rustling and attacks on rural communities.

Some militant jihadists have also operated in the region. An alleged militant camp in Sokoto state was the target of a US airstrike on 25 December last year.

Katsina has been one of the states most affected by the violence.

Local media reported that the retired officer had been going to a wedding on 30 May when armed men attacked his vehicle and seized him, his wife and their driver.

Days before news of his death emerged, a video shared on social media appeared to show Abubakar in captivity. He was seen with an apparent injury to his left leg alongside his wife and other hostages.

The military said it chose not to comment publicly on the abduction while efforts to free those in captivity were being made.

"In deference to ongoing rescue efforts by security agencies, the Armed Forces withheld public comment while every operational resource was deployed in the hope of securing his safe return," the statement said.

The whereabouts and condition of Abubakar's wife remain unknown. But a military spokesman said that "ongoing operations have since been further intensified to bring perpetrators to justice and to dismantle all terrorist networks threatening our nation".

The military paid tribute to the major general, who local media reported was 61 when he died, describing the loss as "tragic" and offered condolences to his family and former colleagues.

A statement said he made "immense contributions to counter-insurgency operations… His commitment to duty and to the unity of Nigeria remains a shining example for all personnel."

[Lähde: Leadership]
The Katsina State Government has announced the death of retired Major General Rabe Abubakar while in the custody of bandits, describing the incident as a tragic loss to his family, the state, and the nation.

LEADERSHIP reports that retired General Rabe was one-time Director of Defence Information (DDI) at the Defence Headquarters (DHQ) of Nigeria. His death comes just days after he, alongside his kidnapped wife, appeared in a viral video in which he was pleading to the State government to heed to the bandits’ demands in exchange for his freedom.

In a statement issued on Saturday by the Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr. Nasiru Muazu, the State government said the retired senior military officer died from complications arising from diabetes and hypertension during his captivity.

The government expressed deep sorrow over the development, noting that extensive efforts were made by the state government and security agencies to secure the ex-Army General’s release to no avail.

“It is with profound sadness that we confirm the General’s death while in bandits’ captivity. Despite the relentless and concerted efforts of the State Government and various security agencies to secure his safe release, the situation ended in this tragedy,” the statement said.

According to the government, the late General’s abduction and subsequent death represented a significant loss not only to his immediate family and Katsina State but also to Nigeria as a whole.

Governor Dikko Umaru Radda extended his condolences to the family of the deceased and the nation, describing the incident as a dark moment that underscored the need for stronger collaboration in tackling insecurity.

The governor said the tragedy serves as a reminder of the urgent need for a collective and intensified response against criminal elements threatening peace and security across communities.

The state government reiterated its commitment to working closely with the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that those responsible for the abduction are brought to justice.

It also assured residents that efforts to combat banditry and restore lasting peace across the state would continue unabated.

The government offered prayers for the repose of the late General’s soul and comfort for his family during the difficult period of mourning.

payload.title: Siepattu nigerialainen eläköitynyt kenraali kuoli vankeudessa
payload.summary: Eläkkeellä ollut kenraalimajuri Rabe Abubakar on kuollut sieppaajiensa hallussa Luoteis-Nigeriassa. Tapaus korostaa Katsinan osavaltion ja laajemmin alueen vakavia turvallisuusongelmia.
payload.content:
Eläkkeellä ollut nigerialainen kenraalimajuri Rabe Abubakar on kuollut vankeudessa sen jälkeen, kun aseistautuneet miehet sieppasivat hänet Luoteis-Nigeriassa. Abubakar siepattiin vaimonsa kanssa Katsinan osavaltiossa viime kuussa, ja hänen kuolemastaan ovat kertoneet sekä maan armeija että Katsinan osavaltion viranomaiset.

## Sieppaus tapahtui matkalla häihin

Paikallisten tietojen mukaan Abubakar oli matkalla häihin 30. toukokuuta, kun aseistetut miehet hyökkäsivät hänen ajoneuvoonsa. Hyökkääjät veivät mukanaan Abubakarin, hänen vaimonsa ja kuljettajan.

Abubakar oli aiemmin toiminut näkyvässä tehtävässä Nigerian armeijan tiedottajana vuosina 2015–2017. Leadershipin mukaan hän oli myös puolustushallinnon tiedotuksesta vastannut johtaja Nigerian puolustusesikunnassa.

Katsinan osavaltion hallinto kuvasi kuolemaa raskaaksi menetykseksi Abubakarin perheelle, osavaltiolle ja koko maalle. Osavaltion sisäisestä turvallisuudesta vastaavan viranomaisen mukaan eläkkeellä ollut korkea-arvoinen upseeri kuoli vankeuden aikana diabetekseen ja korkeaan verenpaineeseen liittyneisiin komplikaatioihin.

## Video levisi ennen kuolinuutista

Abubakarin ja hänen vaimonsa kerrottiin esiintyneen ennen kuolinuutista sosiaalisessa mediassa levinneellä videolla, jossa Abubakar vetosi viranomaisiin sieppaajien vaatimusten täyttämiseksi. Toisissa tiedoissa videon kerrottiin näyttäneen hänet vankeudessa vaimonsa ja muiden panttivankien rinnalla. Hänen vasemmassa jalassaan näytti olevan vamma.

Nigerian asevoimat kertoi pidättäytyneensä julkisista kommenteista sieppauksen aikana, koska turvallisuusviranomaiset yrittivät edelleen vapauttaa panttivankeja. Armeijan mukaan pelastustoimiin käytettiin operatiivisia resursseja siinä toivossa, että Abubakar saataisiin takaisin elossa.

## Katsina kärsii väkivallasta

Mikään ryhmä ei ole ilmoittautunut sieppauksen tekijäksi. Luoteis-Nigeriassa rikollisjengit, joita paikallisesti kutsutaan usein bandiiteiksi, ovat tehneet sieppauksia lunnaita varten sekä karjavarkauksia ja hyökkäyksiä maaseutuyhteisöihin.

Katsina kuuluu osavaltioihin, joita väkivalta on koetellut erityisen paljon. Alueella on lähdetietojen mukaan liikkunut myös jihadistisia aseellisia toimijoita. Viime vuoden 25. joulukuuta Yhdysvaltain ilmaisku kohdistui väitettyyn militanttileiriin Sokoton osavaltiossa, joka sijaitsee samalla Luoteis-Nigerian laajemmalla turvallisuusalueella.
summary_bullets: Eläkkeellä ollut kenraalimajuri Rabe Abubakar kuoli sieppaajiensa hallussa Luoteis-Nigeriassa.
Hänet siepattiin vaimonsa ja kuljettajan kanssa Katsinan osavaltiossa 30. toukokuuta.
Alueella rikollisjengit tekevät usein lunnassieppauksia ja hyökkäyksiä maaseutuyhteisöihin.

A retired Nigerian army general who had been kidnapped by gunmen in the country's north-west has died while being held captive, the military has said. Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar, who had a high-profile job as military spokesman between 2015 and 2017, was abducted with his wife while travelling in Katsina state last month. No group has said it was behind the kidnappings. The abduction and death of Abubakar highlights the continuing security challenges facing parts of north-west Nigeria, where criminal gangs known locally as "bandits" frequently carry out kidnappings for ransom, as well as cattle rustling and attacks on rural communities. Some militant jihadists have also operated in the region. An alleged militant camp in Sokoto state was the target of a US airstrike on 25 December last year.

Maj Gen Rabe Abubakar's death highlights continuing security challenges facing parts of the country.

The Katsina State Government has announced the death of retired Major General Rabe Abubakar while in the custody of bandits, describing the incident as a tragic loss to his family, the state, and the nation. LEADERSHIP reports that retired General Rabe was one-time Director of Defence Information (DDI) at the Defence Headquarters (DHQ) of Nigeria. His death comes just days after he, alongside his kidnapped wife, appeared in a viral video in which he was pleading to the State government to heed to the bandits’ demands in exchange for his freedom. In a statement issued on Saturday by the Commissioner for Internal Security and Home Affairs, Dr. Nasiru Muazu, the State government said the retired senior military officer died from complications arising from diabetes and hypertension during his captivity.

Katsina has been one of the states most affected by the violence. Local media reported that the retired officer had been going to a wedding on 30 May when armed men attacked his vehicle and seized him, his wife and their driver. Days before news of his death emerged, a video shared on social media appeared to show Abubakar in captivity. He was seen with an apparent injury to his left leg alongside his wife and other hostages. The military said it chose not to comment publicly on the abduction while efforts to free those in captivity were being made. "In deference to ongoing rescue efforts by security agencies, the Armed Forces withheld public comment while every operational resource was deployed in the hope of securing his safe return," the statement said.
